nl:
A smart-home door-lock network coordinates firmware-update time slots for a fleet of locks. Two independent controller instances run concurrently and draw from one shared pool of update slots. To claim a slot, an instance performs a compare-and-swap on a per-slot register: it only succeeds if the register currently reads empty, in which case the register is stamped with the lock's identity and a grant record is logged. If the register is already taken the instance abandons that attempt, increments its retry counter, and may pick a fresh lock and slot later. A lock that holds a slot may release it, which clears the register and removes the grant. Because both instances share the same register pool, the compare-and-swap is the only thing preventing two different locks from believing they own the same slot. Every logged grant must therefore agree with what the register actually holds.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a grant record says a lock holds a given slot, that slot's register still names exactly that lock, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two different locks.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Locks, Slots, Insts, NONE, MaxTries
ASSUME NONE \notin Locks
VARIABLES reg, place, tgt, grants, tries

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Slots -> Locks \cup {NONE}]
    /\ place \in [Insts -> Locks \cup {NONE}]
    /\ tgt \in [Insts -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ grants \subseteq (Locks \X Slots)
    /\ tries \in [Insts -> 0..MaxTries]

Init ==
    /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ place = [i \in Insts |-> NONE]
    /\ tgt = [i \in Insts |-> NONE]
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ tries = [i \in Insts |-> 0]

Held(l) == \E s \in Slots : <<l, s>> \in grants

Begin(i, l, s) ==
    /\ place[i] = NONE
    /\ tries[i] < MaxTries
    /\ ~Held(l)
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![i] = l]
    /\ tgt' = [tgt EXCEPT ![i] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, grants, tries>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ place[i] # NONE
    /\ tgt[i] # NONE
    /\ reg[tgt[i]] = NONE
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![tgt[i]] = place[i]]
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {<<place[i], tgt[i]>>}
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
    /\ tgt' = [tgt EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED tries

Retry(i) ==
    /\ place[i] # NONE
    /\ tgt[i] # NONE
    /\ reg[tgt[i]] # NONE
    /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
    /\ tgt' = [tgt EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, grants>>

Release(l, s) ==
    /\ <<l, s>> \in grants
    /\ reg[s] = l
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ grants' = grants \ {<<l, s>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, tgt, tries>>

Reset(i) ==
    /\ place[i] = NONE
    /\ tries[i] > 0
    /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, place, tgt, grants>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Insts, l \in Locks, s \in Slots : Begin(i, l, s)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Reset(i)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Retry(i)
    \/ \E l \in Locks, s \in Slots : Release(l, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, place, tgt, grants, tries>>

NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A l \in Locks, s \in Slots :
        (<<l, s>> \in grants) => reg[s] = l
====

nl:
A container-ship crane yard runs several cranes that stack containers into bays. A global epoch counter labels the current configuration; a reconfiguration action bumps the epoch and reassigns cranes to bays wholesale. Each bay accumulates a container count, and the yard as a whole has a hard total capacity that the sum of all bay loads must never exceed. A crane may load a container into its assigned bay only while the yard's total load is still below capacity, or unload one it previously placed. Any crane may crash silently at any moment, after which it performs no more work, though the containers it already stacked remain in place. A crashed crane can later be repaired and rejoin. Reconfiguration and crashes interleave freely, so the capacity check on loading is the only guard that keeps the yard within its limit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of container loads across all bays is always less than or equal to the yard's total capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od7m9p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Cranes, Bays, Cap, MaxEpoch, MaxMoves, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Bays
VARIABLES epoch, assign, load, alive, moves

RECURSIVE Sum(_)
Sum(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN load[x] + Sum(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ assign \in [Cranes -> Bays \cup {NONE}]
    /\ load \in [Bays -> 0..Cap]
    /\ alive \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ moves \in 0..MaxMoves

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ assign = [c \in Cranes |-> NONE]
    /\ load = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ alive = [c \in Cranes |-> TRUE]
    /\ moves = 0

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \E f \in [Cranes -> Bays \cup {NONE}] : assign' = f
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, alive, moves>>

Load(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ assign[c] # NONE
    /\ moves < MaxMoves
    /\ Sum(Bays) < Cap
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![assign[c]] = @ + 1]
    /\ moves' = moves + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign, alive>>

Unload(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ assign[c] # NONE
    /\ load[assign[c]] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![assign[c]] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign, alive, moves>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign, load, moves>>

Repair(c) ==
    /\ ~alive[c]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assign, load, moves>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Load(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Unload(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Repair(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, assign, load, alive, moves>>

WithinCapacity == Sum(Bays) <= Cap
====

nl:
An elevator bank moves passengers between floors. Passengers wait on floors or ride in cars, and the total headcount is fixed: nobody is ever created or destroyed, only relocated. Each floor carries a version number used for optimistic concurrency control. A car first reads a floor and records that floor's current version. It may then board one waiting passenger only if the recorded version still matches the floor's live version; on a successful board it moves one passenger from the floor into the car and bumps the floor's version. If the version has since changed the car abandons the read and must read again before retrying. A car may also let one passenger alight onto a floor, which likewise bumps that floor's version. Cars can crash silently and stop working, and may later be repaired. The version-matching discipline is what keeps two cars from double-servicing the same waiting passenger.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of passengers waiting on floors plus riding in cars always equals the fixed initial headcount.

---- MODULE W4Od6m0p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Floors, Cars, Total, MaxVer, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Floors
VARIABLES atFloor, inCar, ver, lock, rver, alive

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ atFloor \in [Floors -> 0..Total]
    /\ inCar \in [Cars -> 0..Total]
    /\ ver \in [Floors -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ lock \in [Cars -> Floors \cup {NONE}]
    /\ rver \in [Cars -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ alive \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ atFloor = [f \in Floors |-> IF f = CHOOSE g \in Floors : TRUE THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ inCar = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ ver = [f \in Floors |-> 0]
    /\ lock = [c \in Cars |-> NONE]
    /\ rver = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ alive = [c \in Cars |-> TRUE]

Read(c, f) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ lock[c] = NONE
    /\ lock' = [lock EXCEPT ![c] = f]
    /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![c] = ver[f]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atFloor, inCar, ver, alive>>

Board(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ lock[c] # NONE
    /\ LET f == lock[c] IN
        /\ atFloor[f] > 0
        /\ ver[f] = rver[c]
        /\ ver[f] < MaxVer
        /\ atFloor' = [atFloor EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
        /\ inCar' = [inCar EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
        /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ lock' = [lock EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rver, alive>>

Retry(c) ==
    /\ lock[c] # NONE
    /\ ver[lock[c]] # rver[c]
    /\ lock' = [lock EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atFloor, inCar, ver, rver, alive>>

Alight(c, f) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ inCar[c] > 0
    /\ ver[f] < MaxVer
    /\ inCar' = [inCar EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ atFloor' = [atFloor EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, rver, alive>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atFloor, inCar, ver, lock, rver>>

Repair(c) ==
    /\ ~alive[c]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atFloor, inCar, ver, lock, rver>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : Read(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Board(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Retry(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : Alight(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Repair(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<atFloor, inCar, ver, lock, rver, alive>>

Conserved == SumF(atFloor, Floors) + SumF(inCar, Cars) = Total
====

nl:
An airport baggage router uses two-level hierarchical locking. The concourse is divided into zones, and each zone contains several chutes; a chute is identified by its zone together with a slot. To work a chute, a router must first take the coarse lock on the enclosing zone, then the fine lock on the specific chute; the fine lock can only be taken by whoever already holds the zone's coarse lock. A router holding a chute's fine lock may serve bags through it, up to a bounded amount. Locks are released fine-first, and a router may only drop a zone's coarse lock once it holds no fine lock inside that zone. A privileged admin override can be switched on to hand a chute's fine lock to a router directly, bypassing the hierarchy; while the override is on the discipline is suspended, and the override may only be switched back off once every held fine lock is once again backed by the matching coarse lock. This keeps stale routers, ones that lost their zone lock, from continuing to act.
SAFETY PROPERTY: unless the admin override is active, any router holding a chute's fine lock also holds the coarse lock of that chute's zone.

---- MODULE W4Od17m8p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Routers, Zones, Slots, MaxServe, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Routers
Chutes == Zones \X Slots
ZoneOf(ch) == ch[1]
VARIABLES coarse, fine, adminOn, served

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Zones -> Routers \cup {NONE}]
    /\ fine \in [Chutes -> Routers \cup {NONE}]
    /\ adminOn \in BOOLEAN
    /\ served \in [Chutes -> 0..MaxServe]

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [z \in Zones |-> NONE]
    /\ fine = [ch \in Chutes |-> NONE]
    /\ adminOn = FALSE
    /\ served = [ch \in Chutes |-> 0]

AcquireCoarse(r, z) ==
    /\ coarse[z] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![z] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, adminOn, served>>

AcquireFine(r, ch) ==
    /\ fine[ch] = NONE
    /\ coarse[ZoneOf(ch)] = r
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![ch] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, adminOn, served>>

Serve(r, ch) ==
    /\ fine[ch] = r
    /\ served[ch] < MaxServe
    /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![ch] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, adminOn>>

ReleaseFine(r, ch) ==
    /\ fine[ch] = r
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![ch] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, adminOn, served>>

ReleaseCoarse(r, z) ==
    /\ coarse[z] = r
    /\ \A ch \in Chutes : ZoneOf(ch) = z => fine[ch] # r
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![z] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, adminOn, served>>

AdminGrant(r, ch) ==
    /\ adminOn
    /\ fine[ch] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![ch] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, adminOn, served>>

AdminOn ==
    /\ ~adminOn
    /\ adminOn' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, served>>

AdminOff ==
    /\ adminOn
    /\ \A ch \in Chutes : fine[ch] # NONE => coarse[ZoneOf(ch)] = fine[ch]
    /\ adminOn' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, served>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Routers, z \in Zones : AcquireCoarse(r, z)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, ch \in Chutes : AcquireFine(r, ch)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, ch \in Chutes : Serve(r, ch)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, ch \in Chutes : ReleaseFine(r, ch)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, z \in Zones : ReleaseCoarse(r, z)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, ch \in Chutes : AdminGrant(r, ch)
    \/ AdminOn \/ AdminOff

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, fine, adminOn, served>>

Authorized ==
    adminOn \/ (\A ch \in Chutes : fine[ch] # NONE => coarse[ZoneOf(ch)] = fine[ch])
====

nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch moves money between member banks. Every bank holds a balance, and the grand total across all banks is a conserved quantity: settlement only relocates funds, never mints or burns them. A single shared settlement register acts as a compare-and-swap lock. A bank first proposes a one-unit transfer naming a source and a destination bank. To execute it, the bank compare-and-swaps the settlement register from free to its own identity; only one bank can hold it at a time. Holding the register, it settles the proposed transfer by debiting one unit from the source and crediting one to the destination, then bumps a settlement version and releases the register. A holder may also abort, releasing the register without moving money. Any bank may crash silently and stop proposing or settling, and may later be repaired. The atomic debit-and-credit is what preserves the total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of all member-bank balances always equals the fixed initial total.

CONSTANTS Banks, Total, MaxVer, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Banks
Pairs == Banks \X Banks

SumF(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

    /\ bal \in [Banks -> 0..Total]
    /\ reg \in Banks \cup {NONE}
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ prop \in [Banks -> Pairs \cup {NONE}]
    /\ alive \in [Banks -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ bal = [b \in Banks |-> IF b = CHOOSE c \in Banks : TRUE THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ reg = NONE
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ prop = [b \in Banks |-> NONE]
    /\ alive = [b \in Banks |-> TRUE]

Propose(b, from, to) ==
    /\ alive[b]
    /\ prop[b] = NONE
    /\ from # to
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![b] = <<from, to>>]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, reg, ver, alive>>

Acquire(b) ==
    /\ alive[b]
    /\ reg = NONE
    /\ prop[b] # NONE
    /\ reg' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, ver, prop, alive>>

Settle(b) ==
    /\ reg = b
    /\ prop[b] # NONE
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ LET from == prop[b][1]
           to == prop[b][2]
       IN /\ bal[from] > 0
          /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![from] = @ - 1, ![to] = @ + 1]
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ reg' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED alive

Abort(b) ==
    /\ reg = b
    /\ reg' = NONE
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, ver, alive>>

Crash(b) ==
    /\ alive[b]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, reg, ver, prop>>

Repair(b) ==
    /\ ~alive[b]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, reg, ver, prop>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks, from \in Banks, to \in Banks : Propose(b, from, to)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Acquire(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Settle(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Abort(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Crash(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Repair(b)

nl:
A container-ship crane yard uses two-phase commit to move containers out of one shared staging pool into bays. Two independent transaction instances run at once and both draw from the same pool. A transaction begins by choosing a target bay and entering a voting phase, provided the pool is non-empty. Each participant crane then casts a yes vote. Once every participant has voted yes the transaction commits, atomically taking one container from the shared pool and adding it to the target bay. A transaction in the voting phase may instead abort, moving nothing. After committing or aborting a transaction resets to idle and can run again. Separately, a container can be returned from any bay back to the pool. Because both transaction instances decrement the same pool, the non-empty guard is what stops the pool from going negative, and no step ever changes the total number of containers in the yard.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared pool count plus the sum of all bay counts always equals the fixed total number of containers.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Txns, Bays, Parts, Total
VARIABLES pool, bay, state, target, yes

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ bay \in [Bays -> 0..Total]
    /\ state \in [Txns -> Phases]
    /\ target \in [Txns -> Bays]
    /\ yes \in [Txns -> SUBSET Parts]

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ bay = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ state = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ target = [t \in Txns |-> CHOOSE b \in Bays : TRUE]
    /\ yes = [t \in Txns |-> {}]

Begin(t, b) ==
    /\ state[t] = "idle"
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![t] = b]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, bay>>

Vote(t, p) ==
    /\ state[t] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin yes[t]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, bay, state, target>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ state[t] = "voting"
    /\ yes[t] = Parts
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![target[t]] = @ + 1]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<target, yes>>

Abort(t) ==
    /\ state[t] = "voting"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, bay, target, yes>>

ResetTxn(t) ==
    /\ state[t] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, bay, target, yes>>

ReturnToPool(b) ==
    /\ bay[b] > 0
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, target, yes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Txns, b \in Bays : Begin(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Txns, p \in Parts : Vote(t, p)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Abort(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : ResetTxn(t)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : ReturnToPool(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<pool, bay, state, target, yes>>

Conserved == pool + SumF(bay, Bays) = Total
====

nl:
A print-shop job spooler allocates spool slots to print jobs using two-phase commit. Each slot has at most one owning job. A job starts idle, then proposes a desired slot and enters a voting phase. Participant workers each cast a yes vote. Once all participants have voted yes, the job commits: provided the desired slot is still unowned, the slot's owner becomes that job and the job records the slot as held. A privileged admin override lets a job commit its desired slot without waiting for the votes, but it still refuses to hand out a slot that is already owned. A voting job may abort instead, and committed or aborted jobs reset back to idle. A job holding a slot may release it, clearing both the ownership and its own record. The unowned-slot guard on both the normal and the admin commit is what prevents the same slot from being handed to two jobs.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a job records a slot as held, that slot's owner is exactly that job, so no slot is ever allocated to two different jobs at once.

---- MODULE W4Od11m2p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Jobs, Slots, Parts, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Jobs
VARIABLES owner, want, held, phase, yes

Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Jobs \cup {NONE}]
    /\ want \in [Jobs -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ held \in [Jobs -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ phase \in [Jobs -> Phases]
    /\ yes \in [Jobs -> SUBSET Parts]

Init ==
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ want = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]
    /\ held = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]
    /\ phase = [j \in Jobs |-> "idle"]
    /\ yes = [j \in Jobs |-> {}]

Propose(j, s) ==
    /\ phase[j] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "voting"]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![j] = s]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, held>>

Vote(j, p) ==
    /\ phase[j] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin yes[j]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![j] = @ \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, want, held, phase>>

Commit(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = "voting"
    /\ yes[j] = Parts
    /\ want[j] # NONE
    /\ owner[want[j]] = NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![want[j]] = j]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![j] = want[j]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<want, yes>>

AdminCommit(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = "voting"
    /\ want[j] # NONE
    /\ owner[want[j]] = NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![want[j]] = j]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![j] = want[j]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<want, yes>>

Abort(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = "voting"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "aborted"]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]

nl:
A subway signalling system divides the track into blocks, and safety requires that no block ever holds more trains than its capacity, classically one. A global epoch counter names the current signalling configuration; a reconfiguration bumps the epoch and re-declares, wholesale, which blocks are open for entry. A train may enter a block only when that block is open and its occupancy is still below capacity; a train may leave a block that is occupied. A privileged admin override can be switched on and off. While the override is on, an operator may force a block open, or admit a train into a closed block, but even the override never lets a block exceed its capacity. Reconfiguration, ordinary movements, and admin actions all interleave. The capacity guard, present on both ordinary and override entry, is the sole thing keeping any block within its limit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every block's occupancy is always less than or equal to its fixed capacity.

nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator runs two independent allocator instances that draw runway assignments from one shared pool. A global round counter tracks reconfigurations. To claim a runway, an instance proposes it and collects ballots from controllers; each ballot is stamped with the round in which it was cast. An instance may commit its claim only when it has gathered a quorum of ballots stamped with the current round and the runway is still unowned; on commit it records the round of commitment and takes ownership. A reconfiguration bumps the global round, which makes all previously cast ballots stale, so an in-flight proposal must gather fresh current-round ballots before it can commit. A committed instance may release its runway, and a proposing instance may abort. Because a commit is only valid when backed by a quorum of non-stale ballots, no allocation is ever made on the authority of too few, or out-of-date, controllers.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every committed allocation is backed by at least a quorum of controller ballots stamped with that allocation's own commit round.

nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler hands out operating-room time slots to surgical teams under committee approval. Each slot may be held by at most one team. A team requests a specific slot and then gathers approvals from committee members; members are slow but never fail, so an approval may arrive at any time and in any order, and none is ever lost. A team books its requested slot only once it has a quorum of approvals and the slot is still unheld: it then stamps the slot with its identity and records the slot as its booking. A booked team may cancel, clearing both the slot's stamp and its own record, and a still-seeking team may withdraw. Because a booking is only finalized against an unheld slot, and each slot carries a single holding stamp, a team's recorded booking always matches the slot's stamp.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a team records a slot as its booking, that slot is stamped with exactly that team, so no slot is booked by two teams at once.

nl:
A library book-reservation system lets patrons reserve individual copies using optimistic concurrency control. Each copy carries a version number and, at most, one reserving patron. A patron who holds no reservation first reads a copy, recording that copy's current version. The patron may then reserve that copy only if it is still unreserved and its version still matches what was read; a successful reservation stamps the copy with the patron, records the copy as the patron's held reservation, and bumps the copy's version. If the version has moved on since the read, the patron abandons the attempt and must read again. Patrons are slow but never fail, so reads and reserve attempts may be arbitrarily delayed but are never lost. A patron may return the copy it holds, clearing the stamp and its record and bumping the version. The version match is what stops two patrons from reserving the same copy.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a copy is stamped with a reserving patron, that patron records this exact copy as held, so no copy is reserved for two patrons at once.

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet works shelves organized into aisles, using two-level hierarchical locking. An aisle lock is capacity-limited rather than exclusive: up to some number of robots may hold a given aisle at once, and that capacity can be changed at runtime. A shelf lock is exclusive. A robot may join an aisle only while that aisle has spare capacity, and may take a shelf's exclusive lock only while it currently holds the enclosing aisle. Holding a shelf lock, a robot may pick items from it up to a bounded amount. Locks are released shelf-first: a robot may drop an aisle only when it holds no shelf in that aisle. Aisle capacities may be raised or lowered at any time, but lowering never evicts robots that already hold the aisle. The requirement that a shelf holder currently belongs to the aisle's holder set is what keeps a robot that never joined, or that has left, the aisle from acting on its shelves.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every robot holding a shelf's exclusive lock is currently a member of that shelf's aisle holder set.

    /\ Cardinality(aisleHolders[a]) < cap[a]
    /\ aisleHolders' = [aisleHolders EXCEPT ![a] = @ \cup {r}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, shelf, picks>>

    /\ r \in aisleHolders[AisleOf(sh)]
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![sh] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleHolders, cap, picks>>

    /\ picks[sh] < MaxPick
    /\ picks' = [picks EXCEPT ![sh] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleHolders, cap, shelf>>

DropShelf(r, sh) ==

    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![sh] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleHolders, cap, picks>>

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser controls the dispensing of prescriptions, where actually dispensing a prescription is irreversible and must happen at most once, even across refill workflows. Each prescription carries a single-fill quota, initially one, and a compare-and-swap claim register naming the pharmacist currently handling it. A pharmacist claims an open prescription by compare-and-swapping the register from empty to their identity, moving it to the claimed state. From the claimed state the pharmacist may dispense, but only while the fill quota is still positive: dispensing decrements the quota, marks the prescription dispensed, and clears the register. A pharmacist may instead cancel a claim, returning the prescription to open. A privileged admin override, when active, can dispense directly, bypassing the claim but still honoring the quota, and can reopen a dispensed prescription for a refill workflow without restoring its quota. The positive-quota guard on every dispense path is therefore the only thing preventing a second, illegitimate dispense.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no prescription's remaining fill quota ever drops below zero, so the irreversible dispense happens at most once per prescription.

A power-grid load shedder maintains one shared record of which load tokens have been shed. Two independent controller instances update this record concurrently using optimistic concurrency control, and both draw tokens from the same shared pool. The record is a set of shed tokens carrying a version number, and a separate durable ledger tracks every token that has been successfully committed. An instance begins an update by choosing a token not yet in the record and snapshotting both the current record contents and its version. To commit, it writes back its snapshot together with its new token, but only if the record's version still matches the one it snapshotted; the commit bumps the version and records the token in the durable ledger. If the version has changed, the instance abandons the attempt and re-snapshots. An external consumer may drop a token from both the record and the ledger. The version match on commit is exactly what prevents one instance's stale write from silently discarding a token another instance already committed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every token in the durable committed ledger is still present in the shared record, so no committed update is ever lost.

nl:
A power-grid load shedder tracks the total amount of load currently shed in one shared accumulator, guarded against exceeding a hard capacity limit. Several controllers adjust the accumulator concurrently using optimistic concurrency control; the controllers are slow but never fail, so their read and commit steps may be arbitrarily delayed yet none is ever dropped. The accumulator carries a version number. A controller begins by snapshotting the accumulator value and version and choosing how much additional load to shed. To commit it writes back its snapshot plus that increment, but only if the version still matches its snapshot and the resulting total would stay within capacity. A successful commit updates the accumulator and advances the version. If the version has moved, the controller re-snapshots and tries again. Load may also be restored, decrementing the accumulator. The capacity check on every commit is the sole guard that keeps the shared total within the limit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared shed-load accumulator never exceeds the fixed capacity limit.

CONSTANTS Ctrls, Cap, MaxTotal, Step, MaxVer, NONE
ASSUME MaxTotal >= Cap
VARIABLES total, ver, rsnap, rver, want

TypeOK ==
    /\ total \in 0..MaxTotal
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ rsnap \in [Ctrls -> 0..MaxTotal]
    /\ rver \in [Ctrls -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ want \in [Ctrls -> {NONE} \cup 1..Step]

    /\ total = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ rsnap = [c \in Ctrls |-> 0]
    /\ rver = [c \in Ctrls |-> 0]
    /\ want = [c \in Ctrls |-> NONE]

Bump(v) == IF v = MaxVer THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

Begin(c, d) ==
    /\ want[c] = NONE
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![c] = d]
    /\ rsnap' = [rsnap EXCEPT ![c] = total]
    /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![c] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, ver>>

Commit(c) ==
    /\ want[c] # NONE
    /\ ver = rver[c]
    /\ rsnap[c] + want[c] <= Cap
    /\ total' = rsnap[c] + want[c]
    /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rsnap, rver>>

    /\ ver # rver[c]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, ver, rsnap, rver>>

    /\ want[c] # NONE
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, ver, rsnap, rver>>

    /\ total' = total - 1
    /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rsnap, rver, want>>

    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Retry(c)

A library book-reservation system is replicated across several nodes that elect a leader to serialize writes into a shared durable store of committed reservation requests. Client reservation requests arrive into an unordered in-flight pool, so the leader may pick them up in any order. Only the current leader may apply a pending request: applying it moves the request from the pool into the durable store and records it as acknowledged to the client. Leadership can fail over: the leader may step down, after which a new leader is elected in a higher term. Failover must never lose an acknowledged reservation. An in-flight request may time out and be dropped from the pool before any leader applies it. A committed request may later be consumed, which removes it from both the durable store and the acknowledgement ledger together. Because stepping down and re-electing a leader leave the durable store untouched, and applies only ever add, every reservation once acknowledged to a client stays in the store across any number of failovers and reorderings.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every request recorded as acknowledged is present in the durable store, so no committed reservation is ever lost across leader failover.

    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ store = {}
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ acked = {}

Elect(r) ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ leader' = r
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, inflight, acked>>

StepDown ==

    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, store, inflight, acked>>

Submit(req) ==
    /\ req \notin inflight
    /\ req \notin store
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {req}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, store, acked>>

    /\ acked' = acked \cup {req}

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm feeds surveillance tasks through a bounded work queue with backpressure. The queue holds at most a fixed capacity of tasks. Producers submit tasks into the queue only while it is below capacity; when the queue is full, backpressure kicks in and a submission is instead rejected, bumping a bounded rejection tally rather than growing the queue. Because the swarm processes tasks out of order, any drone may pull any queued task, not just the oldest, which removes it from the queue and puts it into that drone's service slot. A drone finishing its task marks it done. Completed tasks can later be recycled so their identifiers become available for new submissions again. Each task sits in exactly one place at a time: waiting in the queue, in service at a drone, or done. The below-capacity guard on submission, together with the reject-on-full path, is what keeps the queue from ever exceeding its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of tasks waiting in the work queue never exceeds the queue's fixed capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od14m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Tasks, Drones, Cap, MaxRej, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Tasks
VARIABLES queue, inService, done, rejected

Located(t) ==
    \/ t \in queue
    \/ \E d \in Drones : inService[d] = t
    \/ t \in done

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in SUBSET Tasks
    /\ inService \in [Drones -> Tasks \cup {NONE}]
    /\ done \in SUBSET Tasks
    /\ rejected \in 0..MaxRej

Init ==
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ inService = [d \in Drones |-> NONE]
    /\ done = {}
    /\ rejected = 0

Enqueue(t) ==
    /\ ~Located(t)
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, done, rejected>>

Reject(t) ==
    /\ ~Located(t)
    /\ Cardinality(queue) = Cap
    /\ rejected < MaxRej
    /\ rejected' = rejected + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inService, done>>

Assign(d, t) ==
    /\ inService[d] = NONE
    /\ t \in queue
    /\ inService' = [inService EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ queue' = queue \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, rejected>>

Complete(d) ==
    /\ inService[d] # NONE
    /\ done' = done \cup {inService[d]}
    /\ inService' = [inService EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, rejected>>

Recycle(t) ==
    /\ t \in done
    /\ done' = done \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inService, rejected>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Enqueue(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Reject(t)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, t \in Tasks : Assign(d, t)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Complete(d)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Recycle(t)

A network of vending machines shares one critical resource, a common coin vault, that only a single machine may access at a time. The machines run a leader election with failover: at any moment at most one machine is the elected leader, tagged by an election term. Only the current leader may enter the critical section to access the vault; while inside it may perform bounded vend operations, then it exits. A leader may step down and relinquish leadership, but only once it is no longer inside the critical section, after which another machine can be elected in the same or a later term. Machines are slow but never fail, so a machine may take arbitrarily long to enter, vend, or exit, but it never crashes and never vanishes mid-operation. Because entry is gated on being the sole current leader, and a leader must leave the critical section before handing off leadership, no two machines are ever inside the critical section at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a machine is inside the critical section, it is the current elected leader, so at most one machine ever holds the critical resource.

An air-traffic runway allocator issues takeoff clearances to flights, where actually clearing a flight for takeoff is irreversible and must happen at most once per flight. Each clearance is agreed through two-phase commit among the controlling participants, the tower and ground control. A flight starts idle; beginning its clearance moves it into a voting phase and resets the collected votes, while a bounded attempt counter records how many times it has been put up for clearance. Each participant then casts a yes vote; the participants are slow but never fail, so a vote may be arbitrarily delayed yet is never lost. A flight is cleared only when every participant has voted yes and its single-clearance budget is still positive; clearing consumes the budget and marks the flight cleared. A voting flight may abort back to idle, and a cleared flight may be reopened for replanning, but reopening never restores the clearance budget. The positive-budget guard on the clearance step is therefore the sole thing preventing a flight from being cleared for takeoff a second time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no flight's clearance budget ever drops below zero, so the irreversible takeoff clearance happens at most once per flight.

    /\ p \notin yes[f]

A pharmacy prescription dispenser has a bank of dispensing heads, each a critical resource that no two pharmacists may use at the same time. Heads can be taken online or offline at runtime, so the pool's usable capacity changes over time. Pharmacists acquire a head using optimistic concurrency control: a pharmacist first reads a head and records that head's current version, then attempts to acquire it. The acquire succeeds only if the head is currently unheld, online, and its version still matches what was read; on success the pharmacist becomes the head's holder, begins using it, and the head's version advances. If the version has changed the pharmacist abandons the attempt and reads again. A pharmacist using a head may release it, clearing the holder and advancing the version. A head may be switched online or offline at any moment. The unheld-head check on acquire is the sole guard ensuring that a pharmacist only ever uses a head it exclusively holds.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a pharmacist is using a dispensing head, that pharmacist is the head's sole holder, so no head is ever used by two pharmacists at once.

---- MODULE W4Od16m0p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Heads, Pharm, MaxVer, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Pharm
VARIABLES online, ver, holder, rhead, rver, using

Bump(v) == IF v = MaxVer THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

    /\ online \in [Heads -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ ver \in [Heads -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ holder \in [Heads -> Pharm \cup {NONE}]
    /\ rhead \in [Pharm -> Heads \cup {NONE}]
    /\ rver \in [Pharm -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ using \in [Pharm -> Heads \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ online = [h \in Heads |-> TRUE]
    /\ ver = [h \in Heads |-> 0]
    /\ holder = [h \in Heads |-> NONE]
    /\ rhead = [p \in Pharm |-> NONE]
    /\ rver = [p \in Pharm |-> 0]
    /\ using = [p \in Pharm |-> NONE]

Read(p, h) ==
    /\ rhead[p] = NONE
    /\ using[p] = NONE
    /\ rhead' = [rhead EXCEPT ![p] = h]
    /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![p] = ver[h]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<online, ver, holder, using>>

Acquire(p) ==
    /\ rhead[p] # NONE
    /\ using[p] = NONE
    /\ LET h == rhead[p] IN
        /\ holder[h] = NONE
        /\ online[h]
        /\ ver[h] = rver[p]
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![h] = p]
        /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![p] = h]
        /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![h] = Bump(@)]
    /\ rhead' = [rhead EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<online, rver>>

    /\ rhead[p] # NONE
    /\ ver[rhead[p]] # rver[p]
    /\ rhead' = [rhead EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<online, ver, holder, rver, using>>

        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![h] = NONE]
        /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![h] = Bump(@)]
    /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<online, rhead, rver>>

SetOnline(h, b) ==
    /\ b # online[h]
    /\ online' = [online EXCEPT ![h] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, holder, rhead, rver, using>>

    \/ \E p \in Pharm : Acquire(p)
    \/ \E p \in Pharm : Retry(p)
    \/ \E p \in Pharm : Release(p)
    \/ \E h \in Heads, b \in BOOLEAN : SetOnline(h, b)

An air-traffic runway allocator assigns runway slots to inbound flights under controller quorum. Each slot may be allocated to at most one flight. A flight requests a specific slot and enters a seeking phase, collecting yes votes from controllers. Controllers are slow but never fail: a vote may arrive at any time, and a controller that has voted may even retract its vote before the decision is made, but no controller ever drops out entirely. A flight is assigned its requested slot only once it holds a quorum of current votes and the slot is still unallocated; assignment records the slot as the flight's and marks the slot allocated to that flight. A seeking flight may withdraw, and an assigned flight may release its slot, clearing both records. Because assignment is gated on the slot being unallocated, and each slot records a single allocatee, whatever flight a slot is allocated to is exactly the flight that holds that slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a slot is allocated to a flight, that flight has that slot recorded as its assignment, so no slot is allocated to two flights at once.

    /\ alloc \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {NONE}]
    /\ assigned \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ want \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ votes \in [Flights -> SUBSET Controllers]
    /\ phase \in [Flights -> States]

    /\ alloc = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ assigned = [f \in Flights |-> NONE]
    /\ want = [f \in Flights |-> NONE]
    /\ votes = [f \in Flights |-> {}]
    /\ phase = [f \in Flights |-> "idle"]

Request(f, s) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "seeking"]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![f] = s]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![f] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, assigned>>

CastVote(f, c) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "seeking"
    /\ c \notin votes[f]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![f] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, assigned, want, phase>>

Retract(f, c) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "seeking"
    /\ c \in votes[f]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![f] = @ \ {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, assigned, want, phase>>

    /\ want[f] # NONE
    /\ alloc[want[f]] = NONE
    /\ Cardinality(votes[f]) >= Quorum
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![want[f]] = f]
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![f] = want[f]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "assigned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<want, votes>>

Withdraw(f) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "seeking"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, assigned, want, votes>>

Release(f) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "assigned"
    /\ assigned[f] # NONE
    /\ alloc[assigned[f]] = f
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![assigned[f]] = NONE]
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![f] = NONE]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<want, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots : Request(f, s)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, c \in Controllers : CastVote(f, c)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, c \in Controllers : Retract(f, c)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Assign(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Withdraw(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)

An elevator bank keeps a shared dispatch record mapping each service key to its latest committed value. Several dispatch coordinators update this record concurrently using two-phase commit, and a separate acknowledgement map records, per key, the value most recently acknowledged as committed to clients. A coordinator begins a write by choosing a key and a value and entering a voting phase with its vote set cleared. Each participant then casts a yes vote. Once all participants have voted yes, the coordinator commits, writing the value into both the shared record and the acknowledgement map for that key. A privileged admin override lets a coordinator force its pending write through without the votes, but it too writes the record and the acknowledgement together. A voting coordinator may abort, and a committed one resets to idle. Because every commit path updates the shared record and the acknowledgement map in lock step, the record for any key never falls out of sync with its last acknowledged value.
SAFETY PROPERTY: for every key that has an acknowledged value, the shared record holds exactly that value, so no acknowledged update is ever lost.

    /\ phase[o] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin yes[o]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![o] = @ \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, ack, phase, wkey, wval>>

Commit(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "voting"
    /\ yes[o] = Parts
    /\ wkey[o] # NONE
    /\ rec' = [rec EXCEPT ![wkey[o]] = wval[o]]
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![wkey[o]] = wval[o]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wkey, wval, yes>>

AdminForce(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "voting"
    /\ wkey[o] # NONE
    /\ rec' = [rec EXCEPT ![wkey[o]] = wval[o]]
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![wkey[o]] = wval[o]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wkey, wval, yes>>

Abort(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "voting"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, ack, wkey, wval, yes>>

ResetCoord(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "committed"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, ack, wkey, wval, yes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Coord, k \in Keys, v \in Vals : Begin(o, k, v)
    \/ \E o \in Coord, p \in Parts : Vote(o, p)
    \/ \E o \in Coord : Commit(o)
    \/ \E o \in Coord : AdminForce(o)
    \/ \E o \in Coord : Abort(o)
    \/ \E o \in Coord : ResetCoord(o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<rec, ack, phase, wkey, wval, yes>>

NoLostUpdate == \A k \in Keys : ack[k] # NONE => rec[k] = ack[k]

nl:
An elevator bank admits boarding requests into cars, each of which has a bounded passenger capacity that must never be exceeded. Admitting a passenger requires approval by a quorum of dispatch controllers. A boarding request starts idle, then targets a specific car and enters a seeking phase with no votes yet. Controllers are slow but never fail, so their approval votes may arrive in any order and at any time, and none is ever lost. A request boards its target car only once it has gathered a quorum of votes and that car's occupancy is still below capacity; boarding increments the car's occupancy. A seeking request may withdraw back to idle, and a boarded passenger may alight, decrementing the car's occupancy. Because boarding is gated on the target car being below its capacity, no car's occupancy ever rises above its limit no matter how the votes and movements interleave.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every car's passenger occupancy is always less than or equal to its fixed capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od6m5p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Reqs, Cars, Controllers, Quorum, Cap, MaxOcc, NONE
ASSUME MaxOcc >= Cap
States == {"idle", "seeking", "boarded"}
VARIABLES occ, phase, target, votes

TypeOK ==
    /\ occ \in [Cars -> 0..MaxOcc]
    /\ phase \in [Reqs -> States]
    /\ target \in [Reqs -> Cars \cup {NONE}]
    /\ votes \in [Reqs -> SUBSET Controllers]

Init ==
    /\ occ = [ca \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [r \in Reqs |-> "idle"]
    /\ target = [r \in Reqs |-> NONE]
    /\ votes = [r \in Reqs |-> {}]

Request(r, ca) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "seeking"]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = ca]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED occ

Vote(r, c) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "seeking"
    /\ c \notin votes[r]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, phase, target>>

Board(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "seeking"
    /\ target[r] # NONE
    /\ Cardinality(votes[r]) >= Quorum
    /\ occ[target[r]] < Cap
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![target[r]] = @ + 1]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "boarded"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<target, votes>>

Withdraw(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "seeking"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, target, votes>>

Alight(r) ==
    /\ phase[r] = "boarded"
    /\ target[r] # NONE
    /\ occ[target[r]] > 0
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![target[r]] = @ - 1]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<target, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reqs, ca \in Cars : Request(r, ca)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs, c \in Controllers : Vote(r, c)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Board(r)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Withdraw(r)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Alight(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<occ, phase, target, votes>>

WithinCapacity == \A ca \in Cars : occ[ca] <= Cap
====

nl:
A container-ship crane yard moves containers between one staging pool and several bays, coordinated by an elected leader crane. The total number of containers in the yard is conserved: every move only relocates a container, never creates or destroys one. Move requests, either load-from-pool-into-a-bay or unload-a-bay-back-to-pool, accumulate in an unordered pending set, so the leader may service them in any order. Only the current leader crane may apply a pending request: applying a load takes one container from the pool and adds it to the named bay, while applying an unload takes one from the named bay and returns it to the pool; each applied request is removed from the pending set. Leadership can fail over, with the leader stepping down and another crane being elected in a later term; failover leaves the pool and bay counts untouched. Because both apply steps move exactly one container from one place to another, and failover moves nothing, the yard's total never changes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the staging pool count plus the sum of all bay counts always equals the fixed total number of containers.

---- MODULE W4Od7m3p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Cranes, Bays, Total, MaxEpoch, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Cranes
Moves == {"load", "unload"} \X Bays
VARIABLES leader, epoch, pool, bay, pending

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Cranes \cup {NONE}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ bay \in [Bays -> 0..Total]
    /\ pending \in SUBSET Moves

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ bay = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ pending = {}

Elect(cr) ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ leader' = cr
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxEpoch THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, bay, pending>>

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # NONE
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pool, bay, pending>>

SubmitLoad(b) ==
    /\ <<"load", b>> \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<"load", b>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, pool, bay>>

SubmitUnload(b) ==
    /\ <<"unload", b>> \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<"unload", b>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, pool, bay>>

ApplyLoad(cr, b) ==
    /\ leader = cr
    /\ <<"load", b>> \in pending
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {<<"load", b>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch>>

ApplyUnload(cr, b) ==
    /\ leader = cr
    /\ <<"unload", b>> \in pending
    /\ bay[b] > 0
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ pending' = pending \ {<<"unload", b>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch>>

Next ==
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes : Elect(cr)
    \/ StepDown
    \/ \E b \in Bays : SubmitLoad(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : SubmitUnload(b)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Bays : ApplyLoad(cr, b)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Bays : ApplyUnload(cr, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, epoch, pool, bay, pending>>

Conserved == pool + SumF(bay, Bays) = Total
====

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network distributes a fixed number of access credentials among holders, such as individual locks or user profiles. The total credential count is conserved: a transfer only moves a credential from one holder to another, never mints or destroys one. Credentials are moved by two-phase-commit transactions. A transaction begins idle, then names a distinct source and destination holder and enters a voting phase with an empty vote set. Participant coordinators each cast a yes vote; participants are slow but never fail, so votes may arrive in any order and be delayed, yet none is ever lost. Once every participant has voted yes and the source still has a credential to give, the transaction commits, debiting one credential from the source and crediting one to the destination. A voting transaction may abort instead, and committed or aborted transactions reset to idle. Because the only state-changing commit debits the source and credits the destination together by one, the total number of credentials in the network never changes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of access credentials across all holders always equals the fixed initial total.

---- MODULE W4Od18m2p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Holders, Total, Txns, Parts, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Holders
Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}
VARIABLES cred, phase, src, dst, yes

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ cred \in [Holders -> 0..Total]
    /\ phase \in [Txns -> Phases]
    /\ src \in [Txns -> Holders \cup {NONE}]
    /\ dst \in [Txns -> Holders \cup {NONE}]
    /\ yes \in [Txns -> SUBSET Parts]

Init ==
    /\ cred = [h \in Holders |-> IF h = CHOOSE g \in Holders : TRUE THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ src = [t \in Txns |-> NONE]
    /\ dst = [t \in Txns |-> NONE]
    /\ yes = [t \in Txns |-> {}]

Begin(t, s, d) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "idle"
    /\ s # d
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
    /\ src' = [src EXCEPT ![t] = s]
    /\ dst' = [dst EXCEPT ![t] = d]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED cred

Vote(t, p) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin yes[t]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, phase, src, dst>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ yes[t] = Parts
    /\ src[t] # NONE /\ dst[t] # NONE
    /\ cred[src[t]] > 0
    /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![src[t]] = @ - 1, ![dst[t]] = @ + 1]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<src, dst, yes>>

Abort(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, src, dst, yes>>

ResetTxn(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, src, dst, yes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Txns, s \in Holders, d \in Holders : Begin(t, s, d)
    \/ \E t \in Txns, p \in Parts : Vote(t, p)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Abort(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : ResetTxn(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<cred, phase, src, dst, yes>>

Conserved == SumF(cred, Holders) = Total
====
